documents.title: Learn About Generative AI: Vassar AI Guidelines
documents.summary: A library research guide stating that Vassar has no official generative AI policy and leaves policy to faculty and departments. It gives short student advice: check the course policy, ask the professor, disclose use, verify outputs, and mind privacy.
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Vassar College does not have an official policy on generative AI but rather empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies', so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors: delegates.

units.why: Framing sentence: the guide exists 'to support Vassar community members as they navigate decisions', so it states scope and purpose of the guidance; informs, general phase, institution-level framing (P56).
units.anchor: designed to support Vassar community members as they navigate decisions
units.policy: The guide supports Vassar community members as they navigate decisions about their use of generative AI.
units.fit_note: Also acknowledges the topic is rapidly evolving (P54 flavour) without committing to review or feedback.
units.resolution_why: A and B both chose P56 for the purpose sentence. A also coded 'rapidly evolving' as a separate P54 unit; the source only acknowledges change and promises no review or feedback, so that unit is dropped and its point kept here as a fit note.

units.why: 'Vassar College does not have an official policy on generative AI' states there is no AI-specific policy, exactly the content of P108.
units.anchor: Vassar College does not have an official policy on generative AI

units.why: 'empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies about AI for their courses' hands the decision to instructors and departments, so P04 (per-instructor) rather than P85, since there is no university rule for units to depart from.
units.anchor: empowers Vassar faculty members and departments to make tailored policies about AI for their courses
units.resolution_why: A: informs; B: may (permission to departments). The source says the College 'empowers' faculty and departments to make policies, which describes where authority sits rather than addressing a permission to them, so informs; actor admin and P04 agree.

units.why: 'what's permissible in one class might constitute a violation of the Academic Integrity policy in another class' says a course's rule does not carry across courses (P11); it also ties misuse to the Academic Integrity policy, but the main point is course-specificity.
units.anchor: permissible in one class might constitute a violation of the Academic Integrity policy

units.why: 'Check the syllabus and course page on Moodle' directs students to find and follow each course's AI policy, matching P78 (student duty to learn the rules) rather than P10, which is about asking when unsure.
units.anchor: Check the syllabus and course page on Moodle
units.policy: Students check the syllabus and course page on Moodle to familiarize themselves with the course AI policy.

units.why: 'If you have questions about it, or there isn't a policy, talk to your professor' tells students to ask the instructor when unsure or when no policy exists; this is P10 and not P06, since no fallback ban or permission is stated.
units.anchor: If you have questions about it, or there isn't a policy,

units.why: 'make sure to disclose your use of AI' instructs students to acknowledge AI use; the imperative gives a should-level modality given the guide's advisory tone ('As you make decisions'). Type P24 (disclose with submission).
units.anchor: make sure to disclose your use of AI.
units.frag_start: If you use generative AI, make
units.policy: Students who use generative AI make sure to disclose their use of AI.
units.resolution_why: Both give P24/should. B anchors only 'If you use generative AI, make sure to' and codes the example formats as a separate unit; A's anchor carries the full instruction. The examples are part of the same rule.

units.why: 'It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI' strengthens the disclosure rule by asking for transparency about how AI was used; it stays with P24 since no tool or prompt detail (P25) is required.
units.anchor: It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI
units.fit_note: Asks for transparency about how AI was used; examples (citing as a source, describing in Methods) are loose, not a prescribed format, and no required form or tool/prompt details (not P25).
units.resolution_why: Both give P24/should. B's separate unit for example formats ('citing it as a source, describing how you used it in the Methods section', B: may) only illustrates how to disclose, so it is not a separate rule and is dropped; its fit note is kept here.

units.why: 'Critically evaluate the outputs of AI tools' tells students to assess AI output rather than trust it, which is P31.
units.anchor: evaluate the outputs of AI tools
units.resolution_why: B's anchor was just 'Critically', too thin to carry the rule. The source reads 'Critically evaluate the outputs of AI tools'; A's anchor states the rule. Both P31.

units.why: 'Verify claims; whenever possible, go to the source!' asks students to check AI claims against sources, i.e. P31 (verify output).

'Stay informed about the ethical concerns... so that you can make an informed decision about whether to use it' asks students to weigh ethics before deciding to use AI; P118 fits better than P102 because the stated purpose is the decision whether to use.
units.anchor: so that you can make an informed decision about whether to use it.
units.fit_note: Also a duty to stay informed (P102).
units.resolution_why: Phase: A general, B before-course. The advice to stay informed so students can decide whether to use AI is not tied to course set-up, so general. Both P118.

units.why: The AI ROBOT Test is described as prompting users 'to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership, type', helping users evaluate a tool before choosing it (P117).
units.anchor: prompts users to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership, type
units.policy: The guide offers the AI ROBOT Test, an evaluation tool that prompts users to consider a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership and type.
units.resolution_why: Actor: A all, B student. The ROBOT Test sits in the guide's tool-selection section for general readers, not students specifically, so all. Both P117.

units.why: The guide points readers to the Ithaka S+R Generative AI Product Tracker, 'a living document' of products; it directs readers to an outside resource, so P115.
units.anchor: A living document, updated regularly as new products enter the market
units.policy: The guide points readers to the Ithaka S+R Generative AI Product Tracker, a living document updated as new products enter the market.
units.resolution_why: Type: A P115, B P117; actor A all, B student. The passage describes the Ithaka S+R tracker as 'a living document' of products and tells no one to evaluate anything; it points readers to an outside resource, so P115, actor all.

units.why: 'If you use AI tools to search for sources, verify that they are legitimate' allows AI source-finding on condition that students verify the sources, which is P104.
units.anchor: If you use AI tools to search for sources, verify that they are legitimate
units.frag_start: If you use AI tools to search
units.fit_note: Conditions AI-assisted source search on verification; does not explicitly grant permission.
units.resolution_why: Modality: A should, B may. The sentence conditions AI-assisted source search ('If you use AI tools to search for sources') on verifying the sources; the operative verb is 'verify', so should. P104 kept from both coders.

units.why: 'Many AI platforms collect user data and chats to further train their models. Check your account settings to see if you can opt out' is privacy advice to check opt-out settings (P50).
units.anchor: Check your account settings to see if you can opt out
units.policy: Users check their account settings to see whether they can opt out of data collection and training.
units.resolution_why: Phase: A general, B during-work. The tip about account settings is not tied to a stage of coursework, so general. Both should/P50. B also coded the fact that platforms collect user data as its own unit; that sentence is context for this advice, not a separate rule, so dropped.

units.why: 'If you are using a free account, you may have little to no privacy and data protection' informs users of privacy risk on free tiers, P50.
units.anchor: you may have little to no privacy and data protection.
units.frag_start: If you are using a free
units.resolution_why: Actor: A all, B student. The sentence says 'If you are using a free account, you may...', addressed to the reader of the student-facing guidance, so student. Both informs/general/P50.

units.why: 'Gemini is considered a safer AI tool... not shared outside of the college' identifies the college-provided tool as the safer choice, so prefer a vetted tool (P50); P92 not chosen because no instruction to use it is given.
units.anchor: interactions with Gemini through your Vassar account are not shared outside
units.policy: Gemini is considered a safer AI tool; as part of the campus Google suite, interactions with Gemini through a Vassar account are not shared outside of the college, and chats with Gemini with a Vassar account cannot be deleted.
units.fit_note: Describes the campus Gemini as safer without telling users to use only it; also notes chats cannot be deleted.
units.resolution_why: Actor: A all, B student; phase: A general, B during-work. 'your Vassar account' addresses the user and names no coursework stage, so student and general. Both P50; P92 not chosen because the tool is described as safer, not required or recommended.

units.why: The guide offers 'Ask a Librarian' with email, chat, text and consultation for research help, directing students to human support (P72).
units.anchor: Need help with your research? Ask a Librarian!
units.fit_note: General research-help service; not stated as an alternative to AI.
units.resolution_why: Modality: A informs, B may; phase: A general, B during-work. The line lists an available service ('Ask a Librarian'), which is a description, and no coursework stage is named, so informs and general. Both P72.

notes: Library guide, not an administrative policy; thin. No school or computing policy found; course layer deferred. Dropped one A-only unit (P54 'rapidly evolving') and two B-only units (example disclosure formats; fact that platforms collect data), explained in resolution_why of the neighbouring units.
